focus.label: Systematized epidermal nevus
focus.why: Blaschko-linear verrucous plaques classic; sporadic healthy child; infantile onset without blisters; winter worsening.

payload.query: Need lesional skin biopsy histopathology and molecular testing for FGFR3, PIK3CA, and RAS genes, plus brain MRI and skeletal survey results. These are critical to confirm systematized epidermal nevus and exclude epidermal nevus syndrome or other mosaic disorders.

FGFR3/PIK3CA/RAS and brain MRI/skeletal survey remain unavailable, but evidence favors this diagnosis; epidermal nevus syndrome cannot be fully excluded. Key data covered.

payload.report: Infantile-onset Blaschko-linear verrucous plaques, winter worsening, biopsy (hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, papillomatosis, focal epidermolytic hyperkeratosis) support systematized epidermal nevus (0.85). Male sex, no neonatal vesicles, extracutaneous features or seasonality refute incontinentia pigmenti; no blistering/redness makes epidermolytic ichthyosis unlikely. Epidermal nevus syndrome remains possible but low (0.15) without extracutaneous involvement; thus, systematized epidermal nevus.
